As a relative linux noob, I needed to reinstall Mint 17.1. I have /home as a separate partition, so I kept it during the refresh. Using the same user/password, after mounting the original /home, I'm unable to get access to the encrypted partition. I tried ecryptfs-unwrap-passphrase, but it doesn't work (the password is definitely the same). I know now to track the passphrase... Any suggestions?
Yes I did back up, it was out of date, just lost a few files that I would like to get back.
Help....how do I recover encrypted /home without passphrase?

ecryptfs has two pass phrases, a login one, and a mount one. If you have an un-encrypted backup created after the encryption, look for ~/.ecryptfs/wrapped-passphrase. Run ecryptfs-unwrap-passphrase ~/.ecryptfs/wrapped-passphrase on it to see your mount passphrase. Also look in the ~/.Private/ folder.

The wrapped-passphrase (the mount passphrase) is encrypted with the login passphrase.

If you don't have have such a back up, you're probably out of luck.

I don't actually have used ecryptfs... This is what I'm understanding from https://wiki.archlinux.org/index.php/ECryptfs. You need to be careful when using encryption, and have a sound and tested procedure out-of-system in case you get lock out.
